etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French médiéval (“medieval”), from Latin medium (“middle”) +‎ aevum (“age”).

definitions.definition: Of or relating to the Middle Ages, the period from approximately 500 to 1500 AD.

quote.text: Brute force can get you into any apartment if you want to get medieval about it.

quote.citation: 2003, Robert Ludlum, The Janson Directive, page 579:
quote.text: "Oh, what a nifty idea," Collins said dryly. "Get a bunch of angry brothers with a blowtorch and some pliers and get medieval on his ass."

definitions.definition: Having characteristics associated with the Middle Ages in popular, modern cultural perception:
Someone living in the Middle Ages.
A medieval example (of something aforementioned or understood from context).

Thank God for modern remedies: the medievals were often useless or even harmful.
